locked_in: State gaming taxes (~$1.6B a year, estimated) are set by state budget bills; no Nov 3 market prices a tax-rate change in any DraftKings state, and the policy book has no tax-rate rows for NY, PA, NJ, MI, IL or OH
2025 state tax hikes already enacted: NJ online rate to 19.75%, Illinois per-wager fee (Jul 2025), Maryland to 20%, Louisiana to 21.5%
Federal wagering excise tax (0.25% of handle, ~-$134M a year, estimated): no market prices repeal
NJ and VA governors were elected in 2025; Ontario is provincial
weak_links: Predictions spend (+$150M if a federal ban forces DraftKings Predictions to close) is derived by subtraction: management's ~$1B 'core' Adjusted EBITDA vs 2026 guidance of $700-900M. The ban would also end a strategic product; long-run value is not netted

Gambling-loss cap: no public estimate of the handle effect was found (Citizens' analyst calls it negative but unquantified). The 0.5-2% of gaming revenue range is the analyst's assumption, not a source

iGaming sizes (NY +$125M, OH +$100M, MA +$80M) all use one ratio: PA-like spend per adult x DraftKings' ~17% national iGaming share x ~20-25% EBITDA margin after tax. A new state's tax rate (NY bills have proposed 30%+) could halve these

Book row doubted: MA-governor.md gives Healey (who opposes iGaming, block: veto) p 0.07 while Minogue, with no row, gets 0. The candidate who blocks the policy ends up with the higher chance of it; the 0.07 swing points the wrong way
Book row doubted: NY-governor.md gives Hochul and Blakeman the same 0.05 (vague) on iGaming, so the race shows no swing although only Hochul controls the budget she has kept iGaming out of

Nebraska: the Kalshi ballot-measure market is thin (383 contracts on the regulation initiative); both 440 (constitutional authorization) and 441 (regulation) are needed. Size uses an LB 421 fiscal note and a sponsor-commissioned study (Eilers & Krejcik), not a fiscal note for 441 itself
New York prediction-market stop: DraftKings' CEO calls the cannibalization 'de minimis'; the impact is small and the federal preemption fight (CFTC v. New York) may decide it rather than the governor

results.hook: DraftKings is spending roughly $100-300M this year building DraftKings Predictions, its CFTC-regulated sports event contracts.
results.event_plain: Congress bans sports contracts on CFTC-regulated prediction markets in 2026

market.question: Law banning sports prediction markets enacted in 2026?
market.rules_summary: Yes if a law banning CFTC-regulated prediction markets from offering sports contracts, or putting them under state gambling regulation, is signed by Dec 31, 2026.

impact.formula: Management: core business ~$1.0B Adjusted EBITDA in 2026 vs guidance $700-900M, the gap being Predictions spend = $100-300M; a ban closes the sports product and stops most of that spend: ~+$150M central, +$50M if some spend continues on non-sports contracts, +$300M at the top of the gap
impact.timing: 2027, once the product is wound down

results.hook: Since 2026 bettors can deduct only 90% of gambling losses, which taxes high-volume players on money they did not win.
results.event_plain: Congress changes or removes the 90% cap on gambling-loss deductions before 2027

market.question: Will the cap on gambling loss deduction be changed?
market.rules_summary: Yes if a bill that removes or changes the gambling tax provision in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act becomes law before Jan 1, 2027 (the most traded rung; later rungs to 2029 trade at 0.21-0.46).

impact.formula: Gaming revenue $5.63B (Sportsbook $3.83B + iGaming $1.80B) x 1% of play from high-volume bettors restored (range 0.5-2%) = $56M (28-113M) x ~45% flow-through after ~25-30% gaming tax and variable costs = ~$25M a year (13-51M)

results.hook: Nebraska votes on letting its racetrack casinos offer mobile sports betting through up to two online brands each; DraftKings gave about $7M to the campaign.
results.event_plain: Nebraska voters legalize online sports betting

market.question: Will Online Sports Wagering Regulation Initiative pass?
market.rules_summary: Yes if Nebraska's Initiative 441 (online sports wagering regulation: two skins per racetrack, 20% tax) passes. The companion constitutional authorization (440, KXSTATEBALLOTMEASURE-NE26-OSWA) trades at about the same price; both are needed.

impact.formula: Fiscal note for the similar LB 421 (20% tax): $20.4M tax in year 4 / 20% = ~$100M online GGR at maturity (sponsor study: $87M tax over 5 years) x DraftKings ~25% national OSB share = $25M revenue x ~20% EBITDA margin after tax, market access and marketing = ~$5M a year (2-10M)
